title: I drive rideshare on the night shift. Tonight a passenger asked me to take the long way home. His address was my own.
transcript:
I drive rideshare on the night shift. Tonight a passenger asked me to take the long way home. His address was my own. I picked him up outside a bar at one in the morning. Gray coat, no phone out, very polite. He got in the back and said, "Take the long way, please. I like to see the lights."

The app showed his destination, and I felt my stomach drop. It was my street. It was my house number, the one with the cracked blue mailbox.

I asked him, nicely, if he was sure. He said, "Oh yes. I've been home for a while. I just never get to ride in the front."

I kept my eyes on the road. In the mirror, he sat perfectly straight, hands on his knees, and his breath never fogged the window. Not once, in the cold.

I drove in circles for twenty minutes because I couldn't make myself turn onto my own block. He never complained. He only hummed, softly, a lullaby my mother used to sing to me.

Finally I pulled over under a streetlight and turned around to face him.

The back seat was empty. The door had never opened.

My phone buzzed. The app said, "Trip complete." Then my porch camera sent an alert.

Someone was sitting on my front steps, waiting for me to come home.
